risks_fired.fix_hint: No fix warranted at this confidence.

risks_fired.evidence: 5 named sub-steps (branch, append block, read branch name back from git, stage+commit, report SHA) with no in-fence 'No preamble' line and no body primer after the fence per check_prompts.md §17's 4+-sub-step trigger.
risks_fired.fix_hint: A one-line 'No preamble — start with git branch.' or a body line after the fence naming the skim-past cue would close the gap; low-stakes since every sub-step here is mechanical, not a judgment call the preamble could substitute for.

prompts_findings.prompt_lead: Push the current branch and set its upstream.
I want you to take the task we scoped earlier in this session end to end.

risks_fired.evidence: Harm the rule guards against: an unattended run's self-report overstates what shipped, and the student — having walked away — has no artifact-level check to catch the gap. Is the harm actually present and unmitigated here? No, on two independent grounds. (1) check_prompts.md §31's evidence-backed-Debrief carve-out downgrades this pattern when the prompt itself carries a recovery instruction — this fence has one: 'If you get stuck, write what you tried and why it didn't work rather than inventing a way forward,' which forbids exactly the fabrication self-report-inflation causes. (2) This is the file's own stated point (‘send it off plainly and you find out what you can't steer yet’) and matches check_pedagogy.md §19 by name — an M4 un-packaged run is DESIGNED to underdeliver against Claude's own report so the student feels the gap, which check_pedagogy.md §51 (deliberate-antipattern prompts) says a single-file judge will keep flagging but should log as accepted-by-design rather than fix. The very next exercise, fork-the-worktree.md → 'Exercise: Diagnose and re-send,' is the pedagogical rescue for exactly this gap — confirmed by reading its recovery ladder (protected task.md block → reported SHA → merge-base), which only makes sense as a recovery FOR an underdelivering, self-reported first run. Filing REVISE would ask the maintainer to neutralise the one moment the module is built to teach.
risks_fired.fix_hint: Not a fix target. If this ever needs re-litigating, the question for the maintainer is whether the M5 diagnose-and-resend rescue still lands close enough after this prompt that the felt gap gets addressed rather than just remembered as a bad experience — that's a cross-module pacing question, not a prompt-body edit.
